summary: Precompute prefix sums once, so the sum of any range L..R is one subtraction: `prefix[R] - prefix[L-1]` (T12 — prefix sums). That turns up to 10⁵ queries from far too slow into instant.

blocks.title: Read the numbers and Q
blocks.text: N, the numbers on one line, then Q — in the same order as the prompts.

blocks.title: Build the prefix sums
blocks.text: `prefix[i]` is the sum of the first i numbers, with `prefix[0] = 0`. That extra 0 at the front is what lets a query starting at L = 1 work: `prefix[R] - prefix[0]`.

blocks.title: Print the queries header
blocks.text: The program prints `Enter queries:` on its own line before reading the query lines, matching the sample.

blocks.title: Answer each query in O(1)
blocks.text: L and R are 1-based and inclusive, so the sum of positions L..R is everything up to R minus everything before L: `prefix[R] - prefix[L - 1]`. Looping over the range for each query would be up to 10⁵ × 10⁵ = 10¹⁰ steps.

complexity: Time O(N + Q) with N, Q ≤ 10⁵ → about 200,000 steps.
pitfalls: Summing `a[L-1:R]` for every query — too slow for big inputs.
